chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When your brother comes to you, bring him what you have, and when you invite him, exert effort for him.

key_terms.بِمَا عِنْدَكَ: with what is with you (what you possess)
key_terms.فَتَكَلَّفْ لَهُ: so exert effort for him (make effort to provide)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette for hosting a brother or guest?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to define the spiritual and social dimensions of 'ikhlas' (sincerity) within brotherhood. It emphasizes that true hospitality requires not just material generosity ('offering what you have') but also active, eager preparation ('making effort'), reflecting the Shia emphasis on strengthening communal bonds through tangible care and attentiveness.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When you give your brother, so give him with what is with you, and when you invite him, so make efforts for him’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If your brother (in belief) comes to you, then serve him with whatever you have, but if you invite him then you can act formally (as you like).”’
